headline: U.S. Proposes Up-to-25% Tariffs on India
deck: The proposed rate would fall to 17% if New Delhi and Washington conclude a trade deal, Business Standard reported.
body: The United States has proposed tariffs of up to 25% on Indian goods under Section 301, Business Standard reported. [E1] The rate would fall to 17% if India and the United States conclude a trade deal, Business Standard reported. [E1]

The proposal would be calculated net of existing Section 301 duties, according to Business Standard. [E1] The Indian Express reported that USTR determined Indian practices were actionable under Section 301. [E2]

India’s Commerce Ministry said India does not have structural excess capacity in any sector. [E3] The ministry said trade concerns should be handled within the bilateral-trade-agreement negotiations. [E4]

On 26 November, the paper reported USTR’s proposed responsive actions, including additional tariffs subject to public comment and exemptions for certain products. [E5] This notice sets out the proposed India rate and the bilateral-deal condition; it does not establish that the proposed tariffs have taken effect. [E1]

evidence_box.fragment: The Donald Trump administration in the United States (US) on Wednesday proposed imposing tariffs of up to 25 per cent on Indian goods, alleging structural excess capacity, but offered to lower the rate to 17 per cent if New Delhi and Washington conclude a trade deal.

source_note.raw_excerpt: The Donald Trump administration in the United States (US) on Wednesday proposed imposing tariffs of up to 25 per cent on Indian goods, alleging structural excess capacity, but offered to lower the rate to 17 per cent if New Delhi and Washington conclude a trade deal. The office of the US Trade Representative (USTR) has proposed calculating the rate ‘net of existing Section 301 duties’ and said Washington would consider adjustments to account for other Section 301 and Section 232 tariffs.
source_note.provenance_note: Verbatim passages recorded in the story evidence.

evidence_box.fragment: USTR said India’s practices relating to structural excess capacity and production in manufacturing sectors were actionable under Section 301.

source_note.raw_excerpt: The USTR said that it has determined that India’s acts, policies, and practices relating to structural excess capacity and production in manufacturing sectors are ‘unreasonable and burden or restrict U.S. commerce and are therefore actionable under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, as amended (Trade Act)’.
source_note.provenance_note: Verbatim passage recorded in the story evidence.

evidence_box.fragment: India’s Commerce Ministry said it was examining the notice and rejected a finding of structural excess capacity.

source_note.raw_excerpt: In response to the Notice of Initiation and in subsequent proceedings, the Department of Commerce stated that India does not have structural excess capacity in any sector,
source_note.provenance_note: Verbatim passage recorded in the story evidence.

evidence_box.fragment: India said trade-related concerns should be addressed through bilateral trade negotiations.

source_note.raw_excerpt: India and the United States are engaged in negotiations for a Bilateral Trade Agreement. It has been India’s position that any trade-related concerns should be addressed within the framework of these negotiations,
source_note.provenance_note: Verbatim passage recorded in the story evidence.

evidence_box.fragment: USTR proposed responsive actions, including additional tariffs subject to public comment and exemptions for certain products identified in annexes.
